content: I want to export 4 passes in photoshop but I want to export them all to a layered EXP or PSD file. How can I do it without having to save each pass as a seperate action

Yes. Use the Compositor and write a single multilayer EXR. PSD export is not supported in vanilla Blender.

Procedure:

1) Enable passes  
View Layer Properties → Passes → enable the 4 passes you need (or add custom AOVs under “AOV” if required).

2) Compositor setup  
Compositing workspace → enable “Use Nodes”.  
Keep the default Render Layers node.  
Add → Output → File Output.  
In the File Output node:
- File Format: **OpenEXR Multilayer**  
- Color Depth: **32-bit Float** (use 16-bit Half if size matters)  
- Codec: **ZIP (lossless)**  
- Click “+” until you have 4 inputs; rename each input to the exact layer names you want (e.g., Diffuse, Glossy, AO, Emission).  
Wire the corresponding sockets from **Render Layers** (or your AOVs) to those 4 inputs.  
Set a Base Path.

3) Render  
Still: F12 → the File Output node writes one **.exr** with all 4 inputs as separate layers.  
Sequence: Ctrl+F12 → one multilayer **.exr per frame**.

4) Open in Photoshop  
Open the EXR with the ProEXR importer (bundled in recent CC). Each named input appears as its own layer/group.

Yes. PSD: no. Multilayer EXR: yes.

Procedure (vanilla Blender):

1) Enable passes  
View Layer Properties → Passes → enable the 4 you need (e.g., Combined/Beauty, Diffuse Color, Specular, Emission). Add AOVs or Light Groups if needed.

2) Compositor setup  
Compositing workspace → check Use Nodes.  
Add → Input → Render Layers (one per View Layer if applicable).  
Add → Output → File Output.  
In File Output:
• Base Path: set your folder  
• Format: OpenEXR Multilayer  
• Codec: ZIP (lossless) or DWAA; Color Depth: 16-bit (Half) or 32-bit (Float)

3) Wire passes into one EXR  
On File Output, click “+” to add 4 inputs, rename each (Beauty, Diffuse, Specular, Emission).  
Connect the corresponding sockets from Render Layers to those 4 inputs.  
(Do not connect to Composite; the File Output node writes the file directly.)

4) Render  
Render → Render Image/Animation. Blender writes a single .exr containing those 4 layers.

Notes  
• Blender cannot write layered PSD. Convert in Photoshop after import.  
• Photoshop needs ProEXR/EXR-IO to open multilayer EXR as layers; otherwise it flattens.  
• For non-color data (Z, Crypto, normals), keep EXR; don’t normalize; save as 32-bit Float to preserve precision.
Can I do it inside blender vanila with nodes_

Blender (vanilla), Cycles. PSD not relevant. Material only.

Model prep
- Real-world scale. Apply scale (Ctrl+A → Scale).
- Separate meshes: one for glass, one for liquid.
- Liquid intersects the inner glass by ~0.2–0.5 mm; delete the liquid’s top cap to avoid coplanar faces.
- Normals outward on both meshes.

Beer material (liquid)
1) Create a new material on the liquid.
2) Nodes:
   - Principled BSDF → Material Output “Surface”
     - Base Color: pure white
     - Transmission: 1.0
     - Roughness: 0.03–0.08
     - IOR: 1.345
     - Specular: 0.5
   - Volume Absorption → Material Output “Volume”
     - Color (pick one):
       - Pale lager: #FFD36A
       - Golden: #F3C13A
       - Amber: #D0892A
     - Density: 4–12 (increase for darker/thicker look)
   - Optional haze: Add Shader(Volume Absorption, Volume Scatter)
     - Volume Scatter Anisotropy: 0.0–0.2
     - Volume Scatter Density: 0.01–0.05

Node wiring (minimal)
- Principled BSDF → Surface
- Volume Absorption (or Add[Absorption + Scatter]) → Volume

Render settings (Cycles)
- Light Paths: enable Transparent Shadows. Caustics optional; not required for the material itself.
- Filmic color management.

Meniscus (realistic rim)
- Give the liquid a slight upward rim at the glass contact: scale the top loop outward a fraction and move up 0.5–1.5 mm, or use a tiny Solidify (0.5–1 mm) with a bevel on the lip.

Bubbles (material-only, quick)
- Add Voronoi Texture → ColorRamp (tight range) → Bump(Strength 0.02–0.05) → Principled Normal for micro-ripples.
- For rising bubbles, instance small icospheres with a particle system on a hidden emitter inside the liquid; assign a glassy material to the bubbles (Transmission 1.0, IOR 1.0–1.05, Roughness 0.0–0.02).

Eevee notes (if you must)
- Render Properties → Screen Space Reflections → enable Refraction.
- Material → Settings → enable Screen Space Refraction; set Refraction Depth ≈ glass wall thickness.
- Transmission 1.0 still applies; Volume Absorption works but looks flatter than Cycles.

Typical starting values
- Pale lager look: IOR 1.345, Roughness 0.05, Absorption Color #F3C13A, Density 6.
- Darker amber: same IOR, Roughness 0.06, Absorption Color #D0892A, Density 10.

Do not tint Base Color; drive color with Volume Absorption so thickness deepens tone physically.
